The difficulty in this type of puzzle is not objective, for a computer maybe but not for a human brain. All the levels (except the insanely sadistic last level) can be solved with (iirc) less than 6 or 7 moves, it's the brain that makes it difficult sometimes. I believe that the disorienting wrap-around mechanics paired with the symmetry of the levels forces the brain to make the least helpful move some of the times in order to discern some pattern and get a bearing on the objective. I'm really interested in this kind of behavior, when the brain approaches a puzzle the wrong way because it's what makes sense to it. In this comment (https://voat.co/v/gaming/comments/746646/3673092) dentedFord had some issues with level 3, even though level 2 is harder (technically) he though that it was much simpler than the other.

So you see, an objective measure of hardness is quite difficult for me to implement, what's hard for me in one level might be basic to you.

In the level list you can find the number of moves you've made to solve a given difficulty of a level, if you play it again and make fewer moves it will update the number of moves.
